newsitem.title: USA: RTW adopts shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: RTW adopts shareholder rights plan.

text.p: RTW Inc said Monday its board of directors has unanimously adopted a shareholder rights plan designed to ensure that all of the company's shareholders receive fair and equal treatment in the event of any proposal to acquire the company.

The action was not taken in response to an attempt to take over the company. "Except for shares held by my wife and me, which are excluded from the Rights Agreement, the company currently has no shareholder with an interest of 15 percent or more, and we are not aware of any current attempt to take control of the company," said Chairman David Prosser.

"The plan was adopted after extensive consideration by the board and is intended to protect the interests of our shareholders in the event of abusive or unfair takeover tactics. It is not designed to prevent the acquisition of the company on terms beneficial to all shareholders," he said in a statement.

The board declared a distribution of one right for each share of common stock outstanding on June 30, 1997. Each right entitles the holder to purchase 1/100th of a share of a new series of junior participating preferred stock of RTW at an initial exercise price of $85.00.

Initially, the rights will be attached to the common stock and will not be exercisable. They become exercisable only following the acquisition by a person or group, without the prior consent of the RTW board, of 15 percent or more of the company's voting stock, or following the announcement of a tender offer or exchange offer to acquire an interest of 15 percent or more.
In certain specified instances, the rights may be redeemed by the company. If not redeemed, they would expire on April 17, 2007.
